clue.text: Piece Times writer sent in so close to deadline

indicators.note: the Times writer is put inside the other letters, sent into them

parts.note: sic is Latin for so or thus
X is the multiplication sign, read as times
a pen is a writing instrument

indicators.note: the close of a word is its final letter, so only the end of deadline is used

explanation.surface: A journalist files a story at the very last minute before the paper goes to press.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Times writer' reads as a journalist but splits into two pieces. A sixpence was an old British coin, worth six old pennies.
explanation.definitionFit: A sixpence is a coin, and a coin is commonly called a piece, as in a ten-pence piece.

clue.text: A hearty speaker of Arabic upset loved one

indicators.note: in a down clue upset means turned upside down, so the whole run is read backwards

parts.note: a hearty is a sailor, as is a tar
an Omani, from Oman, speaks Arabic

explanation.surface: A jolly Arabic speaker is distressed over a sweetheart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns the whole string A TAR OMANI to give INAMORATA.
explanation.definitionFit: An inamorata is a female lover, a woman who is a loved one.

clue.text: Spot fuel being flogged for a quid

parts.note: a pip is a spot, as on dice or cards

indicators.note: something flogged is beaten about, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone spots petrol being sold off for a pound.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flogged' also suggests sold, and 'quid' a pound, but a quid here is a wad of tobacco.
explanation.definitionFit: A quid is a lump of tobacco for chewing, and a pipeful is a comparable portion of tobacco.

clue.text: "I should lead with jack": something a bridge player will often say

definitions.text: something a bridge player will often say

indicators.note: the jack goes in front, leading the other piece

parts.note: in cribbage the jack of the turned suit is called his nob
I'd is short for I should

explanation.surface: A card player announces they will open with the jack.
explanation.walkthrough: In bridge auctions players say 'no bid' when passing, which they do often.
explanation.definitionFit: No bid is the call a bridge player makes when passing in the auction, a frequent utterance.

clue.text: Reading's first in each period

indicators.note: the letter goes inside the abbreviation
the first letter of Reading is taken

explanation.surface: Reading is the top priority in every lesson.
explanation.definitionFit: An era is a period of history, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Interpret Christmas verse

parts.note: Christmas falls in December, abbreviated Dec
an ode is a lyric poem, a piece of verse

explanation.surface: Someone tries to make sense of the poem inside a Christmas card.
explanation.definitionFit: To decode a message is to interpret its meaning, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Players reportedly stopped chasing after ball

indicators.note: the band piece comes after the dance piece, chasing it

parts.note: a ball is a formal dance

indicators.note: reportedly signals that a word is heard rather than read

parts.note: banned means stopped or prohibited

explanation.surface: Footballers, so the story goes, gave up chasing the ball.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reportedly' gives the sound of BANNED, spelt BAND.
explanation.definitionFit: A dance band is a group of musicians, i.e. players of instruments.

clue.text: What cutter might do at length, overtaking a small boat

indicators.note: overtaking means passing round, so the a is surrounded

parts.note: a cutter, a person or tool that cuts, might carve

explanation.surface: A fast sailing cutter draws level and passes a little boat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cutter' suggests a boat, but here it is something that slices.
explanation.definitionFit: A caravel was a small, light sailing ship of the fifteenth and sixteenth centuries.

clue.text: Teach D-stream

parts.note: a rill is a small stream

explanation.surface: Instructing the lowest set in a streamed school.
explanation.walkthrough: D-stream reads as a school's bottom ability group, a British school term.
explanation.definitionFit: To drill pupils is to teach them by repetition, a near synonym.

clue.text: Insect made very little noise?

parts.note: was can stand in for made, as in it was (made) a success
p, piano, is the musical marking for playing quietly

explanation.surface: A tiny creature that made hardly any sound at all.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the second part is to be read as music notation: P (piano) means softly.
explanation.definitionFit: A wasp is a stinging flying insect, an example of the category.

clue.text: Clever people get away with it

definitions.text: Clever people get away with it

parts.words: Clever people get away with it
parts.note: read 'get away' literally: this is the process by which talented, educated people leave their country to work abroad

explanation.surface: Smart people always seem to escape punishment.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests clever people evading blame; the real sense is clever people emigrating.
explanation.definitionFit: A brain drain is the emigration of skilled and highly educated people, so it is how clever people go away.

clue.text: Secret identity adopted by pair of wrongdoers

parts.note: a con is a convict, one wrongdoer

indicators.note: being adopted by someone means being taken in by them, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a fence is a receiver of stolen goods, a second wrongdoer
ID is the usual short form of identity

explanation.surface: Two criminals take on a hidden new identity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pair of wrongdoers' supplies two separate criminals, not one word for a couple; a fence handles stolen goods.
explanation.definitionFit: A confidence is a secret told in trust, as in sharing a confidence with a friend.

clue.text: New record with piece of music, extract from The Planets

parts.note: an EP is an extended-play record
a tune is a piece of music

explanation.surface: A fresh recording of a movement from Holst's suite.
explanation.walkthrough: The Planets is Holst's orchestral suite; its final movement is about this planet.
explanation.definitionFit: Neptune, the Mystic is a movement of Holst's The Planets, so an extract from the suite.

clue.text: Cheers attendant no end

indicators.note: the word loses its final letter, its end

parts.note: a valet is a personal attendant or manservant

explanation.surface: A servant is toasted endlessly with cheers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no end' drops the last letter T from VALET. Vale is Latin for farewell, used in English as a goodbye.
explanation.definitionFit: Cheers is informal British for goodbye, and vale is a Latin farewell, so both are partings.

clue.text: Trouble doctor had after midwife initiated Caesarean delivery

indicators.note: the trouble and doctor letters come after the midwife letter
only the initial of midwife is wanted, its first letter

parts.note: to ail is to trouble, as in what ails you
a Caesarean section is a surgical operation, an op

explanation.surface: A doctor causes problems after a midwife starts a Caesarean birth.
explanation.walkthrough: The obstetric scene hides a postal one: 'delivery' is mail, not a birth.
explanation.definitionFit: A maildrop is a place or box where mail is delivered, so it serves for a delivery.

clue.text: Are they driven primarily during very hot days?

definitions.text: Are they driven primarily during very hot days?

indicators.note: during means within, so one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: roasters are scorching days, informally

indicators.note: primarily means first of all, so only the initial of driven is used

explanation.surface: A question about whether something is mostly done in a heatwave.
explanation.walkthrough: 'primarily' takes D from 'driven', and 'during' places it inside ROASTERS. Read whole, the clue also describes the open cars.
explanation.definitionFit: Roadsters are open two-seater cars, enjoyed with the roof down in hot weather, so they are driven then.

clue.text: Are highly favoured like most gifted pupils

parts.note: an are is a metric unit of area, abbreviated a
blest means blessed, highly favoured by fortune

explanation.surface: The brightest children in a class are the teacher's favourites.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Are' looks like a verb but is the metric area unit, A.
explanation.definitionFit: The ablest pupils are the most capable, i.e. most gifted ones, a superlative synonym.

clue.text: Illuminate place to land

parts.note: a spot is a place
to light is to land or alight, as a bird does

explanation.surface: Lighting up the place where one is to come down.
explanation.definitionFit: To spotlight something is to illuminate it with a focused beam.

clue.text: Woman's smart hairstyle, trimmed front and back

indicators.note: the phrase smart hairstyle loses letters at both ends, leaving a run from its middle

explanation.surface: A woman shows off a chic haircut that has been cut at front and back.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove the S at the front and IRSTYLE at the back of SMART HAIRSTYLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Martha is a female given name, so it is an example of a woman.

clue.text: Grunted, developing swimming stroke

indicators.note: developing means changing form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A swimmer groans while working on a stroke.
explanation.walkthrough: The trudgen is an old overarm swimming stroke named after John Trudgen.
explanation.definitionFit: The trudgen is a swimming stroke, an overarm stroke with a scissor kick.

clue.text: Loser grounded after getting trounced

indicators.note: being trounced means being thoroughly beaten up, signalling the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A defeated competitor is punished after a heavy loss.
explanation.definitionFit: An underdog is the competitor expected to lose, so it can stand for a loser.

clue.text: Brother bitten by bug? That's ridiculous

indicators.note: being bitten by something means being held in its jaws, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: to bug is to annoy, to rile
a sib or sibling is a brother or sister

explanation.surface: A sibling was stung by an insect, an absurd outcome.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bug' looks like an insect but is the verb meaning annoy.
explanation.definitionFit: Risible means laughable, so something risible is ridiculous.

clue.text: Police run away from rioting group

indicators.note: rioting suggests wild disorder, so the remaining letters are scrambled
taking the run away means the r is removed from the word group

parts.note: r is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: Officers flee from a mob of rioters.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing R from GROUP leaves GOUP, which 'rioting' rearranges. The OGPU was the Soviet secret police of the 1920s and 30s.
explanation.definitionFit: The OGPU was the Soviet state security police force, an example of a police organisation.

clue.text: Shakespeare's world

definitions.meaning: the London playhouse where Shakespeare's company performed
the planet Earth, the sphere we live on

explanation.surface: Shakespeare's whole world.
explanation.definitionFit: The Globe was Shakespeare's theatre, and a globe is also the world itself.

clue.text: In shamefaced way, woman dumps rubbish in city

parts.note: she is a pronoun standing for a woman

indicators.note: the rubbish is placed in the city

parts.note: Ely is a cathedral city in Cambridgeshire
pish is an exclamation meaning nonsense, rubbish

explanation.surface: Embarrassed, a woman fly-tips her refuse inside a city.
explanation.walkthrough: ELY is the crosswords' favourite small English cathedral city.
explanation.definitionFit: Sheepishly means in an embarrassed manner, a synonym for in a shamefaced way.

clue.text: Clout someone who's only just in debt?

definitions.text: someone who's only just in debt?
definitions.meaning: read as ..., one who owes only a penny

explanation.surface: Influence belongs to someone barely in the red.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense is cryptic: P (a penny) plus OWER, someone who owes, the question mark flagging the whimsy.
explanation.definitionFit: Power means influence or clout; jokingly a p-ower owes just a penny.

clue.text: He wrote line about good friend

parts.note: on means about, concerning
a fellow is a companion or friend

explanation.surface: A writer pens a line concerning a dear companion.
explanation.walkthrough: Henry Wadsworth Longfellow was the American poet of Hiawatha.
explanation.definitionFit: Longfellow was a nineteenth-century American poet, so a man who wrote.

clue.text: Drink? Friend's up for it

indicators.note: in a down clue up means read from bottom to top

parts.note: a pal is a friend; the 's stands for is

explanation.surface: A buddy fancies a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: To lap is to drink by scooping with the tongue, as a cat drinks milk.

clue.text: Luggage for one's things

definitions.meaning: personal belongings, as in pack up your possessions and go

explanation.surface: Suitcases are for carrying one's possessions.
explanation.definitionFit: Bags means luggage, and also informally one's belongings, as in grab your stuff.

clue.text: Economist making very important points

parts.note: key means crucial or very important
N, E and S are compass points

explanation.surface: An economist gets to the crucial points.
explanation.walkthrough: John Maynard Keynes was the influential British economist.
explanation.definitionFit: Keynes was a famous British economist, an example of the definition.

clue.text: Tense? Love something to smoke

parts.note: the perfect is a grammatical tense
love means zero in tennis, which looks like the letter o

explanation.surface: A nervous lover reaches for something to smoke.
explanation.definitionFit: A perfecto is a cigar thick in the middle and tapered at both ends, something smoked.
